action: opened the order: Invent one new widget that goes beyond everything in the catalog. One remarkable idea, or none.
person at the terminal: proposed Loupe (loupe-widget), Landmarks (landmarks-widget)
Untapped capability: proposed Subtext (thinking stream via turn.step), Attic (tool.describe deferral), Lens (ui.selection)
Delight: proposed Unsent (unsent-widget), Whose Line (whoseline-widget), Jar (jar-widget)
took the order at ideation

stamped reject on "Subtext": The thinking a hook sees is only what the engine shows live, often a summary or nothing, and matching hedge words against the reply would flag nearly every tool-loop turn, so the card cannot keep its promise of what Claude withheld.

stamped reject on "Attic": The engine already puts MCP tools and its own rarely used tools behind ToolSearch, so the few schemas left to move save little while silently changing which tools Claude reaches for.

stamped reject on "Lens": Not chosen: it is the same idea as Loupe, which states the fullscreen limit and the copy button more exactly; its tool-row source line and colour swatch are folded into Loupe.

stamped reject on "Landmarks": Not chosen: jumping the transcript is new, but its best moment needs rows from long ago that the transcript may no longer keep drawn and prompt row ids that are unconfirmed, so it may refuse exactly when wanted.

stamped reject on "Unsent": Not chosen: a charming joke, but it cannot tell a softened draft from an ordinary rewrite, and it records what the person chose not to say for a novelty that fades after a day.
stamped reject on "Whose Line": A variation on theseus and onthisday that in a solo repository names the same author on every edit and adds a git blame to each one.
stamped reject on "Jar": A phrase counter in a pixel jar is a variation on mirror and flow, built on a joke that current models rarely give it coins for.
named the widget loupe-widget ("Loupe")

stamped pass: Loupe is the first widget that knows what the person is pointing at: selecting a hash, path or symbol in the transcript answers what it is, locally, with no tokens and an API verified in the types file.
